config.title: Image Gallery

intro.title: Image Gallery
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an interactive image gallery using React. You will learn how to manage a list of images with state, allowing users to click through them. The core concept is using React's useState hook to track the current image index and update the display. You will work with JSX to render images and buttons, and event handlers to respond to user clicks. By the end, you'll have a functional gallery that cycles through images with previous and next buttons.
intro.usecase: Image galleries are foundational UI patterns across modern web applications. You'll implement them in e-commerce product displays, social media feeds like Instagram, portfolio websites for artists and photographers, and media-rich dashboards. As a React developer, you'll frequently build reusable gallery components that handle image loading, layout responsiveness, and user interactions. Mastering this pattern prepares you for real-world features like lightbox viewers, filtered collections, and dynamic content grids.

objectives: Initialize a state variable to manage an array of image objects
Implement a component that renders a list of images using the map method
Configure an event handler to update the current image index on click
Apply conditional rendering to display a selected image in a larger view
Construct a gallery layout with thumbnails and a main image display
Integrate image sources and alt text from the state data into the UI
Manipulate the state to cycle through images using previous and next buttons

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary imports for React and state management are added.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import both React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the ImageGallery component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ImageGallery that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define a function called ImageGallery that returns JSX. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the ImageGallery component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a component function that returns an empty div, ready to be filled with gallery content.
successCriteria: A component named ImageGallery is defined and returns an empty div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your component is named exactly 'ImageGallery' and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Remember to define a function named ImageGallery that returns a div.

steps.title: Initialize the image data array
steps.instruction: Inside the ImageGallery component, create a constant array named 'images' containing at least three image objects. Each object should have 'id', 'src', and 'alt' properties.
steps.hint: Define the array directly in the component body, before the return statement. Use numeric IDs and placeholder image URLs like 'https://via.placeholder.com/150'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a static array of image data ready to be displayed later.
successCriteria: An array named 'images' is defined inside the component, containing objects with id, src, and alt properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your array is named 'images' and each object has id, src, and alt properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The array isn't quite right. Create a constant named 'images' with at least three image objects, each having id, src, and alt properties.

steps.title: Initialize state for selected image index
steps.instruction: Inside the ImageGallery component, use the useState hook to create a state variable called selectedIndex and initialize it to 0.
steps.hint: Call useState with the initial value 0 and destructure the returned array into two variables: selectedIndex and a setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for tracking a counter
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable selectedIndex that tracks which image is currently selected, starting with the first image (index 0).
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with initial value 0, and the destructured array includes selectedIndex and a setter function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useState(0) and destructuring the result into [selectedIndex, setSelectedIndex].
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax: you need to call useState(0) inside the component and destructure the returned array.

steps.title: Create handler for previous image
steps.instruction: Create a function named handlePrev that decrements the selectedIndex state, wrapping to the last image when at the beginning.
steps.hint: Define a function that updates the selectedIndex using setSelectedIndex. Use the previous state to calculate the new index, ensuring it wraps to images.length - 1 when the current index is 0.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handlePrev function is defined and ready to be used for navigating to the previous image.
successCriteria: A function named handlePrev is defined, which uses setSelectedIndex to decrement the selectedIndex and wraps to the last image when at index 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it correctly handles wrapping to the last image when at index 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handlePrev function is not defined correctly. Ensure you create a function that updates selectedIndex appropriately.

steps.title: Add main container and title
steps.instruction: In your ImageGallery component, return a div element with a className of 'gallery' that contains an h1 element with the text 'Image Gallery'.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement (return null;) with a JSX structure. Remember to wrap multiple elements in a parent container.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now render a basic structure with a title, ready to hold the gallery content.
successCriteria: The component returns a div with className 'gallery' containing an h1 with the text 'Image Gallery'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a div with className 'gallery' that contains an h1 with exactly 'Image Gallery' as its text content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div with className 'gallery' containing an h1 with the text 'Image Gallery'. Check your JSX syntax and structure.

steps.title: Display the selected image
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add an img element that uses selectedIndex to display the current image from the images array. Use the src and alt attributes from the image object.
steps.hint: Access the current image object using images[selectedIndex], then use its properties for the src and alt attributes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The selected image from the images array will be displayed in the UI using an img element with the correct src and alt attributes.
successCriteria: An img element is added to the return statement that uses images[selectedIndex].src and images[selectedIndex].alt for its attributes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the img element correctly uses images[selectedIndex] to access the current image's src and alt properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The img element isn't properly displaying the selected image. Check that you're using images[selectedIndex] to access the current image object.

steps.title: Add navigation buttons and wire handlers
steps.instruction: Add two button elements inside the main container - one labeled 'Previous' and one labeled 'Next'. Wire the 'Previous' button's onClick to the handlePrev function and the 'Next' button's onClick to the handleNext function.
steps.hint: Place the buttons after the image element. Use the onClick attribute to connect each button to its corresponding handler function.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two buttons labeled 'Previous' and 'Next' appear below the image, and clicking them cycles through the gallery images.
successCriteria: Two button elements with labels 'Previous' and 'Next' are present, each with onClick handlers wired to handlePrev and handleNext respectively.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added buttons, but check that both buttons have the correct labels and onClick handlers wired to the right functions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation buttons are missing or not properly connected. Make sure to add two button elements with onClick handlers that call handlePrev and handleNext.

steps.title: Add thumbnail previews
steps.instruction: Below the main image, add a div that maps over the images array to render small thumbnail images for each item, highlighting the currently selected thumbnail with a CSS class.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the images array to generate an img element for each image. Add a className to conditionally apply styling to the selected thumbnail.
steps.expectedOutcome: The gallery will display a row of small thumbnail images below the main image, with the currently selected thumbnail visually highlighted.
successCriteria: A div containing mapped thumbnail images is added
Each thumbnail has a key attribute
The selected thumbnail has a conditional className (e.g., 'selected')
Thumbnails are clickable to change the selected image
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added thumbnails, but make sure each has a unique key, and the selected thumbnail has a conditional className for highlighting.
steps.feedbackWrong: The thumbnails are not correctly implemented. Check that you're mapping over the images array and conditionally applying a className to the selected thumbnail.
